projects.category: Local dictation and meeting notes for Windows
projects.summary: Raw or modified speech-to-text, voice notes and meeting transcripts for Windows. Keep your words and work on your own computer.
projects.why: Capture a thought, write into a focused text field, or return to a recorded conversation. Keep raw recognized words alongside basic cleanup, with local notes and meeting transcripts in the same workspace.
features: Raw text
Keep recognized text unchanged, including fillers and repetitions. Dictionary replacements and writing-style formatting are bypassed.
Modified text
Remove fillers and repeated starts with basic capitalization, punctuation and your selected writing preferences. No sentence-editing model is needed.
Find the moment, not just the file

Find & act connects optional local semantic retrieval to supporting transcript passages, source tracks and timestamps. It is evidence retrieval, not an open-ended chatbot. Model inference/resource acceptance for this preview remains pending.
Highlights with a source
Lightweight extractive ranking selects original timestamped statements. Double-click a passage to open its source.
Action items you review
Suggested tasks show their original statement, editable owner/date fields and a confirmation checkbox. They become tasks after review.
Bookmark it while it happens
Mark Important, Question or Follow up during recording with Ctrl+Alt+1/2/3, then return to the moment after recording. Physical global-shortcut acceptance is still separate.
Projects, people and tags
Group notes, dictation history and meetings with project labels and tags. Search with project:, person: and tag: filters.
Correction learning you control
Review saved spellings/snippets, see where each rule applies and remove a rule to undo future use. Original conversation words are preserved.
Hands-free development preview

Enroll your voice, select allowed apps and start explicitly. The app pauses on lock or microphone changes; Escape stops listening. Matching can make mistakes and physical desktop acceptance remains pending.
Preview, redact, share
Choose exactly what the PDF contains, exclude personal annotations and redact selected preview text. The original recording is unchanged; audio is neither included nor redacted.
A recovery plan for your notes

Opt into daily local snapshots while the app runs. Encrypted snapshots authenticate their contents and restore previews skip existing IDs. Encryption is tied to the Windows account/PC; ZIP supports migration.
Optional features, visible footprint

Install/remove managed optional runtimes without removing notes. Downloaded packages, installed disk space and measured worker RAM are shown separately when available; unknown measurements stay labeled unknown.
One file. Ready for offline English speech.
The installer includes the Windows app, native speech runtime, English model and uninstaller. Standard installation needs no internet connection, Python, Docker, terminal commands or cloud account.
Speak into your workflow
Hold your chosen shortcut to dictate into the focused text field. Local recognition runs on your computer; personal notes and meeting recordings live in the same workspace.
Your voice. Your orbit.
Drag the floating ball, release it and watch gravity, collisions and rolling friction bring it to rest. Click it to reveal an animated half-circle of readable controls.
Make the ball yours
Choose 19 appearances, from sports balls and solar-system worlds to plain Color and Gradient. Pick any color from a live color range and see both ball and expanded tray before applying.
Choose your gravity
Nine independent gravity environments change falling acceleration and airtime. Selecting an environment plays a bounce sample; replay it whenever you want.
Pick your scale
Separate percentage sliders control closed-ball and expanded-menu sizes. The menu can grow from 100% to 200%, scaling its icon tiles and icons together.
Put your own image in orbit
Browse local folders for a PNG, JPEG, BMP or GIF still image. Notewll keeps a local copy, places it inside the ball and rotates it with the surface.
Notes, meetings and readable sharing
Record microphone audio, computer output or both; review source recordings and timestamps, add editable personal notes, and share a PDF snapshot.
Clear controls, quiet desktop
Black icons sit on white round tiles at 50% opacity. The click-to-open menu collapses when you leave it. Reduced motion, hiding and snoozing remain available.
workflow: Download the 0.10.0 Windows preview installer and accompanying SHA256 checksums. Finish active recordings before updating.
Install and open Notewll. Standard English recognition is included; check your microphone in Practice and test the shortcut in your editor.
Choose Preferences > Writing > Text mode, select Raw text or Modified text and save your preferences.
Write by voice, capture a thought, or record a meeting. Mark important moments and keep original statements separate from your personal annotations.
Use Find & act, review suggested tasks, filter by project/tag/person and return to source audio. Semantic search needs its optional setup.
Preview/redact a PDF, schedule local snapshots, and customize the floating ball, gravity, colors, sizes and local image.
projects.architecture: Native C# WinForms on .NET Framework 4.8 captures Windows microphone and WASAPI output audio. Standard offline English speech uses bundled Vosk. Raw text bypasses cleanup; Modified text applies deterministic cleanup and writing preferences. Accurate recognition, semantic search and voice matching have separate optional local setup paths.
projects.trust: The Windows app processes speech and notes locally. Standard installation and recognition work offline. Meeting audio and original transcripts stay separate from editable personal notes. Optional recognition, semantic search and voice matching have their own setup and acceptance limits. Exported PDFs can be edited externally. Review recognized words before sharing.

guide.start: Download Notewll-Setup-0.10.0.exe, finish active recordings, then open the installer. Standard English speech is bundled and installation preserves notes/preferences. Open Preferences > Writing > Text mode and choose Raw text or Modified text. Check your microphone and test dictation in a focused editor. Optional accurate speech, semantic search and voice matching have separate setup paths. This is an unsigned Windows preview.
faq: What is the difference between Raw text and Modified text?

Raw text keeps recognized words unchanged, including fillers and repetitions. Modified text removes fillers and repeated starts with basic formatting. Both modes run locally without a sentence-editing model.
Does it work offline?

The included standard English speech engine and installation work offline. Optional feature setup needs downloads; local inference can run on installed model files. The browser demo is separate and may use online browser speech services.
Can I search meetings and jump to source audio?
Find & act implements passage retrieval and timestamp/source playback. Semantic search needs optional installation and its model-inference/resource acceptance remains pending in this preview.
Are action items created automatically?
Candidate tasks remain suggestions until you review owner/date/text and confirm them. They link to supporting statements.
Are my private annotations included in exports?
You choose Conversation only, Personal notes only or Full record, preview the text, and redact selections before saving a PDF. Audio is not included or redacted.
Is hands-free safe to leave running everywhere?

Choose an explicit allowed-app list and start it manually. Voice matching is experimental and can make mistakes. Escape pauses it, and lock/device changes pause listening. Desktop acceptance remains pending.
What happens to notes when I update?
The installer preserves local notes, recordings and preferences. Encrypted snapshots require the same Windows account/PC; keep ZIP backups for migration.
Is the installer signed?
This is an unsigned Windows preview. Versioned installer files and SHA256 checksums are published together on GitHub Releases.

releases.notes:
# Notewll 0.10.0 — Speak naturally. Keep the words that matter.

Local dictation, voice notes and meeting transcripts for Windows.

## The headline: two text modes

Choose Raw text to keep recognized words unchanged, or Modified text to remove fillers and repeated starts with basic formatting. Original text remains available for review.

## Everything new in this preview

- Raw text and Modified text are the only text modes. Raw text bypasses cleanup and writing rules; Modified text applies basic cleanup.

- General repeated-prefix and abandoned-start cleanup, straight/curly apostrophe matching and two text modes.
- Find & act across conversations, optional local semantic retrieval with source playback, extractive highlights and reviewable action items.
- Timestamped live bookmarks: Ctrl+Alt+1/2/3 for Important, Question and Follow up.
- Projects, tags and person filters; clear correction-rule scopes and undo through rule removal.
- Experimental enrolled-voice hands-free mode with an app allowlist, visible state, lock/device-change pause and Escape to stop.
- Exact-text PDF preview redaction. Personal notes can be excluded; source audio is not redacted or included.
- Opt-in encrypted daily snapshots, authentication/tamper checks, restore previews and existing-ID protection.
- Managed optional-feature storage information and install/remove actions. Unknown download/RAM measurements stay labeled unknown.
- Current screenshots and an illustrative cleanup animation; the existing customizable physics ball remains.

## Downloads

- **Notewll-Setup-0.10.0.exe**: full Windows x64 installer with standard offline English speech included. Run it to install or update, preserving notes/preferences.
- **Notewll-Setup.exe**: the same installer under a convenient filename.
- **Notewll-Small-Update.zip**: compact update files and instructions for an existing installation. Not a full installer.
- **SHA256SUMS-0.10.0.txt**: checksums for those assets.


## Evidence and preview limits

The text-mode update passed 164 automated checks, with 2 skipped checks and 2 excluded live microphone checks. Original text, saved settings and installer packaging were checked. Physical microphone capture and typing into target applications still require desktop acceptance. This is an unsigned Windows preview.

[Product, demo and screenshots](https://myhai.org/projects/dotflow/) · [User guide](https://github.com/sudheer-050/notewll/blob/main/USER_GUIDE.md) · [Source](https://github.com/sudheer-050/notewll)
Your voice. Your orbit. One-file offline English setup, customizable physics ball, local images, live appearance and gravity previews.

# Notewll 0.8.0 - faster local dictation


- Shortcut dictation now recognizes speech every 250 ms while you speak, including when live insertion is disabled or held modifier keys delay typing.
- Silence, quick shortcut taps and empty recognition results return quietly to idle without warning popups, inserted text or clipboard changes.
- Playground preview no longer clears a computed result when an empty optional result is supplied.
- Existing notes, recordings, shortcuts and preferences are retained. Installer, application metadata and About now report 0.8.0.


Verification: 91 application, installer, speech-worker and regression checks passed; four live microphone/keyboard checks were excluded. Direct empty-result/cancellation checks passed too. The full installer embeds the exact verified 0.8.0 application. A cleanup-preview failure found during packaging was fixed and both preview checks now pass. Real microphone capture returns MMSYSERR 1 in this managed session, and keyboard injection is unavailable. Physical shortcut timing, cross-app insertion and recognition accuracy still need desktop acceptance. The installer is unsigned and the certificate-verified automatic updater remains unconfigured; install this preview manually from GitHub Releases.

See verification/STREAMING_DICTATION.md for the measured scope and remaining checks.

# Notewll 0.7.0

Windows x64, English-only, offline speech after initial setup download.

- PDF-only conversation export with readable scope previews and explicit participant-label wording. Original words remain read-only; external PDF copies are not tamper-proof.
- Responsive export, playback, storage and backup interfaces; separate retention and deleted-record recovery.
- Saved-record review separated from new recording controls; actual saved audio sources only, device/activity feedback and grouped actions.
- Apply/Cancel for device changes; permanent toolbar hiding and snooze respected across note actions.
- Compact Home, contextual recovery, consistent Notewll branding, improved themed tabs/dropdowns, searchable word/snippet forms and explicit correction saving.
- Standard, Chat, Email and conservative Code styles; user-controlled Practice and guided first-use checks.

Verification: 85 automated checks passed, four live checks excluded. Isolated UI checks preserve original words and preferences. See FIX_REPORT_0.7.0.md for all 38 review findings and remaining acceptance work.

The installer is unsigned because no code-signing certificate was provided. Published as an unsigned preview. Installation and live desktop acceptance have not been verified in this managed session. Real microphone/call capture, browser/terminal injection, mixed-DPI pointer behavior, Narrator and consented speech-accuracy comparison require a normal desktop session. The managed session denies those operations. No macOS/mobile/cloud sync release is included.


October 22, 2026 update: renamed the application to Notewll across the UI, setup, shortcuts, exports and documentation. Dictation uses direct typing without reading the target field or an automatic paste retry. Existing LocalDictation data and installation identifiers are retained for upgrades. Shortcut preferences are preserved. The Windows preview installer is unsigned; real cross-app insertion still needs desktop acceptance.

﻿# Notewll / Local Dictation 0.6.1 release notes

Windows x64 preview. This historical installer appears as Local Dictation. The project and current application are now named Notewll.

- Safer native speech-engine shutdown, in-memory dictation retry and clipboard restoration.
- Compact Home actions, recent work, persistent session issues, grouped preferences and first-run guidance.
- Light/Dark/System themes, live system-theme refresh, high-contrast button/list colors, reduced motion and optional voice animation.
- Edge-docked hover toolbar, one-time drag hint and keyboard action menu.
- Continuous per-source meeting recognition, separate meters, pause/resume and explicit device-change recovery.
- Content search, sort by date/title/duration, tags, editable speaker labels that preserve original words, and timestamp playback.
- Local source-quote overview, possible decisions/follow-ups and keyword answers with timestamps. No new AI model, cloud service or invented speaker attribution.
- Previewed export scopes, remembered format, searchable/tagged Unicode PDF, Word/Excel convenience protections and CSV.
- Recently deleted recovery, opt-in retention, size breakdown and atomic note backup. Imports validate all metadata before moving records and never overwrite existing IDs.
- Opt-in startup update checks and manual hash/publisher verification. Unsigned installers are rejected by the updater.

First installation needs internet for the native runtime and small English model; speech afterwards is offline. No Docker, Python installation or cloud account is needed. The setup executable is a bootstrapper, not the whole installed runtime.

This installer is unsigned: no Windows code-signing certificate is configured. It is published as a preview, not a signed automatic update. Document editing restrictions are removable and are not tamper-proof evidence.

Verification: 79 application checks passed, four live checks deselected. Real installed Vosk passed 16-stream concurrent shutdown and continuous both-source silence tests. Synthetic silence, hum, clicks and quiet noise produced no words, with and without the quiet gate. Windows media playback seek/speed/pause/close passed on a fixture.

Remaining acceptance limits: this managed session denies microphone/call capture and keyboard injection, and blocks Windows synthetic speech generation. Human speech accuracy, real calls, terminal/browser insertion, audible playback, mixed-DPI monitors and Narrator still need a normal desktop session. No direct Wispr accuracy comparison was performed. Source-quote review is lexical, not a semantic AI summary or generative Q&A. PDF structure tags are present, without a PDF/UA certification claim. Windows English-only remains the platform scope; no mobile/macOS/cloud sync build is included.

evidence.scope: 119 automated checks passed; four live hardware/desktop checks excluded. Clean isolated bundle extraction loaded the included offline speech engine. Ball checks cover all 171 appearance/gravity combinations and local-image rotation. Full interactive installation and physical desktop capture/insertion remain separate acceptance checks.

projects.summary: A self-hosted AI workspace where conversations, projects, decisions, and explicit memory remain available even when the selected model changes.
projects.why: AI conversations are usually trapped inside one provider and important context disappears into old threads. HGPT keeps the durable parts in a database you control, then supplies relevant context to whichever supported runtime you choose.
features: One workspace, many runtimes
Use local Ollama, installed Codex or Claude CLIs, or a configured OpenAI-compatible API without moving the conversation.
Durable memory
Save confirmed facts explicitly and connect them to projects, topics, conversations, and decisions.
Inspectable recall
See which memories, earlier messages, topics, and provider were used for an answer.
Project and decision records
Give long-running work persistent instructions and record choices with rationale, evidence, alternatives, and status.
Private guest access
A signed random guest identity creates an isolated workspace without requiring an account.
Provider controls
Add compatible providers, validate their model catalogs, and keep saved API keys encrypted.
workflow: Open HGPT and start an isolated guest workspace.
Choose a local, CLI, or API-backed model.
Create a project or conversation and add durable instructions when needed.
Save only the facts and decisions that should persist.
HGPT retrieves relevant context, sends it to the selected runtime, and records the trace with the response.
projects.architecture: The interface is vanilla HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. Express assembles context and streams responses; PostgreSQL is the authority for conversations and memory; local embeddings and topic relationships support recall; Redis serves only ephemeral HAI state. Host-authenticated CLI runtimes are reached through a Unix-domain socket rather than copying their credentials into the application container.
projects.trust: Every query is scoped to its signed-in or guest owner. Guest cookies are HTTP-only and SameSite=Strict. Saved provider keys use AES-256-GCM encryption, compatible provider URLs are screened against private-network and credential-bearing targets, and recalled text is labeled as untrusted context rather than executable instruction.
projects.status: Live on myhai.org and under active development. HGPT is a personal knowledge workspace, not an autonomous truth engine: the user decides what becomes confirmed memory, and model output still needs normal review.
projects.name: HGPT
projects.description: A self-hosted AI workspace where conversations, projects, decisions, and explicit memory remain available even when the selected model changes.

uses: Keep a long-running project
Carry project instructions, confirmed facts, and decisions across conversations and model changes.
Inspect an answer
Review the recalled context and provider trace rather than treating memory as an unexplained black box.
Try without registering
Start an isolated guest workspace and select an available runtime.
requirements: A modern browser and a selected available model runtime.
For self-hosting: Node.js, PostgreSQL, and the repository deployment configuration.
An API-backed runtime needs credentials; a local runtime needs its model installed.
guide.start: Open the live workspace, create a conversation, and select an available model. Add a project when you want instructions and decisions to persist beyond one chat.
faq: Do I need an account?
You can start in a private guest workspace. Keep the same browser identity to return to that workspace.
Does changing models erase my project?
Conversations, explicit memories, and decisions belong to HGPT rather than to one provider. The selected runtime receives relevant context for the next response.
What should I save as memory?
Save facts you have confirmed and want to reuse. Model output and retrieved context can be wrong, so review them before making them durable.

projects.summary: HAI’s conversational assistant for text and hands-free voice chat, available instantly without creating an account.
projects.why: H provides a simple conversational space for quick questions and voice interaction without requiring a separate account or a complicated workspace. The interface is designed to feel direct: open the page, type or speak, and continue the conversation.
features: Text conversation
Ask a question, receive a response, and keep the current conversation moving in a focused chat interface.
Hands-free voice mode
Use the browser’s speech capabilities to talk with H and hear responses aloud.
No account required
Open the assistant directly without registration or a saved HAI Messenger identity.
Personal glossary

Conversation transcript

HAI product knowledge

projects.architecture: H is a browser-based interface served by the HAI backend. It currently uses Google’s Gemini API as an interim model runtime while migration back to a locally hosted model is in progress. Voice input and playback use browser Web Speech capabilities, and user-taught glossary terms stay in local browser storage.
projects.trust: During the current interim configuration, message text is sent to Google’s Gemini API for processing. Browser speech handling can vary by browser and operating system. Glossary entries remain local to the browser, and no HAI account is required to start a conversation.
projects.status: Live on myhai.org. Text and voice modes are available now; the model runtime is temporarily Gemini while the locally hosted runtime is being restored.

faq: Is H AI the same as Hagent?
H AI is a conversational text and voice assistant. Hagent manages projects, issues, specialized agents, and scheduled work.
Is the model running locally?
The current hosted configuration uses Gemini as an interim runtime. Message text is sent to that provider for processing.
Why might voice differ between browsers?
Speech input, voices, and permission handling depend on the browser and operating system. Text chat remains the alternative when speech support is unavailable.

projects.summary: A self-hosted control plane for projects, issues, AI agents, squads, skills, and scheduled autopilots, available through a CLI and a web dashboard.
projects.why: Autonomous work becomes hard to trust when tasks, prompts, provider choices, approvals, and failures are spread across tools. Hagent keeps the work visible as issues and records how every agent run was started, routed, delegated, and completed.
features: New in 0.2.3

Gmail and Google Drive read-only connectors, direct APIs and MCP connections, per-agent account access, smoother Google sign-in, and workflow reliability fixes. Full release details are on the download page.
Issue-driven work
Kanban projects support priorities, labels, sub-issues, comments, due dates, run history, and per-workspace issue keys.
Pluggable runtimes
Cloud APIs, OpenAI-compatible services, local Ollama or LM Studio, and installed AI CLIs share one adapter boundary.
Squad delegation
Supervisors can call specialist agents as bounded tools while preserving the delegation trail.
Autopilots
Cron or webhook triggers can assign matching issues or create recurring work automatically.
Recovery and approvals
Interrupted runs continue with existing work; optional approval pauses a run before it starts.
Auditable memory
Provider-neutral memory, learned skill lessons, usage data, routing decisions, and runtime failover stay inspectable.
workflow: Install Hagent locally and start the dashboard.
Configure a local, API, or installed-CLI runtime.
Create a project, agent, and issue.
Assign the issue directly or let an autopilot select it.
Review the timeline, agent output, tool calls, delegations, and any approval request.
projects.architecture: FastAPI serves the dashboard and API, SQLAlchemy stores local state in SQLite, APScheduler handles autopilots, and a runtime adapter exposes a consistent run interface. The CLI mirrors the same project and issue model, so web and terminal workflows operate on the same records.
projects.trust: Terminal access is optional and disabled by default. When enabled, it uses the operating-system permissions of the Hagent process; a configured working directory is not a security sandbox. Remote access should use accounts plus HTTPS or a private network, and untrusted autonomous work belongs in an OS account, container, virtual machine, or isolated worker.

releases.notes:
Hagent 0.2.3 adds direct Gmail and Google Drive connectors, a unified Connections page, and simpler read-only API setup. Google accounts, APIs, and MCP tools can be assigned to individual agents.

### What's new
- Gmail search/read and Drive search/read, including Google Docs text export.
- Google sign-in after one-time installation setup, encrypted credentials, automatic token refresh, and single-use OAuth state with PKCE.
- API setup with name, endpoint, and key; custom authentication under Advanced.
- Account status and per-agent access management, plus connection tests.
- MCP local commands, remote HTTP/SSE connections, and protected credentials.
- Restart helper that checks for running tasks first.

### Fixes
- Preserve Hagent login when Google redirects back.
- Avoid repeated review/completed tasks in default autopilot matching.
- Keep internal maintenance projects off the main board.
- Improve reassignment, issue discussion context, parent/child verification, and failure reporting.

### Setup notes
Google sign-in requires registering an OAuth app once per installation and enabling Gmail and Drive APIs. Google connectors are read-only. Direct APIs support fixed JSON GET endpoints. Access to connected accounts is explicitly assigned to agents; personal account tokens and local data are not part of this release.

See [connection setup](https://github.com/sudheer-050/hagent/blob/v0.2.3/docs/CONNECTIONS.md) and [the changelog](https://github.com/sudheer-050/hagent/blob/v0.2.3/CHANGELOG.md).

Validation: 358 tests passed, 1 native stdio MCP test skipped because of Windows sandbox pipe restrictions. Wheel and source distribution built successfully.

projects.summary: A private career-search command center that gathers real openings, explains their fit, and keeps applications, follow-ups, and preparation in one workflow.
projects.why: Job searches lose time to duplicate listings, expired roles, vague match scores, scattered notes, and repeated document work. The portal turns that fragmented process into a private, explainable queue of opportunities and next actions.
features: Multi-source collection
Normalize openings from public job APIs and employer career systems into one consistent feed.
Freshness and deduplication
Track source identity and posting freshness so repeated or stale listings do not crowd the queue.
Explainable matching
Rank roles against saved preferences and resume evidence while showing why a position fits.
Application tracking
Keep status, follow-up plans, notes, and the source posting together.
Preparation workspace
Organize role research, interview planning, and truthful document tailoring around a specific opening.
Human checkpoints
Unsupported, uncertain, or consequential submission steps stop for user review.
workflow: Create an account and save the roles, locations, and work preferences that matter.
Upload a resume privately for evidence-based matching.
Review normalized recommendations and the reasons behind each score.
Track selected roles through preparation, application, interview, and follow-up.
Use Hagent-assisted preparation where available, with user confirmation for uncertain steps.
projects.architecture: The production application uses Node.js and PostgreSQL behind the same Docker and Cloudflare ingress stack as HAI. Collection adapters convert different source formats into a canonical job record before matching and workflow state are applied.
projects.trust: Resume and preference data are private account data. The system is designed to assist research and preparation, not to invent qualifications or silently complete uncertain external submissions.
projects.status: Live. Job availability and application links come from external sources and can change after collection, so each opportunity should be confirmed at the employer destination before applying.

guide.start: Open the portal, create or sign in to your account, and set role and location preferences. Add your resume, review match explanations, and shortlist an opening before preparing an application.
faq: Does a match score guarantee a suitable job?
No. The score helps prioritize research. Review requirements, location, eligibility, and the employer posting yourself.
Are applications submitted automatically?
The workflow uses human checkpoints for uncertain or consequential steps. Treat preparation and submission as separate actions.
Why can a listing become unavailable?

projects.summary: An open-source Python library that converts messy, internationally formatted corporate spreadsheets into clean, auditable pandas DataFrames.
projects.why: Business spreadsheets routinely mix currencies, date conventions, accounting negatives, totals, identifiers, and error cells. One silent conversion can invalidate an analysis. BizPack centralizes those repairs and records what changed.
features: Spreadsheet cleanup
Normalize columns, totals rows, blank structures, spreadsheet error values, and common export artifacts.
International numbers
Parse currency symbols, thousands and decimal conventions, percentages, and accounting negatives.
Safer identifiers

Date handling
Resolve mixed and ambiguous date formats with explicit controls instead of silent guesses.
Business analysis helpers
Use XLOOKUP-style joins, Pareto analysis, period growth, run-rate forecasting, and related workflows.
Audit trail
Preserve source files and report transformations so a cleaned dataset remains reviewable.
workflow: Install the package from PyPI.
Load an Excel or CSV export into the BizPack workflow.
Inspect detected types and choose any needed locale or date assumptions.
Clean and validate the DataFrame without overwriting the source.
Use the result in pandas or continue with the included business-analysis helpers.
projects.architecture: BizPack is a Python package built around pandas and NumPy with an optional Streamlit interface. The package exposes focused cleaning and analysis operations so it can fit into notebooks, scripts, or repeatable data pipelines.
projects.trust: The library favors explicit, auditable transformation over destructive in-place editing. Ambiguous dates and identifiers need domain context, so results should be reviewed before financial or operational decisions.
projects.status: Published on PyPI as an open-source package. The repository contains installation instructions, usage examples, tests, and the detailed feature reference.

projects.summary: A natural-language classification pipeline that maps corporate business descriptions into a 145-category hierarchical industry taxonomy.
projects.why: Company descriptions are unstructured and inconsistent, while investment research needs stable industry categories. This capstone tests whether a transparent classical NLP pipeline can turn those descriptions into useful hierarchical labels.
features: Domain-aware preparation
Clean descriptions and fill missing text using business-domain signals.
Rich text features
Represent descriptions with word and phrase TF-IDF features spanning one to three grams.
Balanced classification
Use class-weighted linear support-vector models for uneven industry categories.
Hierarchical evaluation
Measure performance across the taxonomy rather than treating every label as unrelated.
Top-three predictions
Return several likely industries for a new description instead of hiding uncertainty.
Reproducible experiments
Keep preprocessing, training, and documented evaluation together in the project.
workflow: Prepare labeled company descriptions and the GECS hierarchy.
Normalize and vectorize the text with TF-IDF.
Train class-balanced linear classifiers.
Evaluate macro-level and hierarchical performance.
Enter a new business description to inspect its three most likely categories.
projects.architecture: The project uses a scikit-learn text pipeline: domain-specific preprocessing, 1-to-3-gram TF-IDF features, and LinearSVC classification. The classical approach keeps training practical and makes feature behavior easier to inspect than a large opaque model.
projects.trust: Industry predictions support research and screening; they are not authoritative classifications. Sparse descriptions, mixed business models, and underrepresented categories can produce uncertain results, which is why multiple candidate labels are exposed.
projects.status: Completed as a DePaul capstone. The strongest documented experiment reached approximately 0.83 macro F1; repository materials provide the implementation and project context rather than a hosted production service.

projects.summary: A free, self-hosted messenger with encrypted real-time chat, media sharing, voice notes, in-chat games, groups, and ephemeral Nearby conversations.
projects.why: Everyday messaging should not require advertising profiles or surrender of conversation content. HAI explores a privacy-first communication stack that can be hosted and operated independently.
features: Encrypted direct messages
Hybrid RSA-OAEP and AES-256-GCM envelopes keep message bodies as ciphertext while passing through the server.
Real-time communication
Socket.IO delivers messages, typing state, presence, read state, and live interaction updates.
Media and voice
Send photos, documents, voice notes, camera captures, and view-once media.
In-chat games
Invite the active contact into Tic Tac Toe, Connect Four, Hangman, trivia, and other live games.
Nearby chat
Enter an anonymous, time-limited conversation mode without adding the other person as a contact.
Installable experience
Use the responsive web client as an installable PWA on desktop or mobile.
workflow: Create and verify an account, then sign in.
Add a contact, join a group, or enter Nearby mode.
The browser encrypts supported direct-message content for the recipient.
The server relays real-time ciphertext and short-lived interaction events.
The recipient decrypts the content in their authenticated browser session.
projects.architecture: Express serves the web application and account APIs, Socket.IO handles live events, PostgreSQL stores durable account and message records, and Redis supports ephemeral coordination. Docker Compose runs the supporting services, while Cloudflare Tunnel provides public HTTPS without opening inbound ports.
projects.trust: Direct messages use browser-side hybrid encryption, but transport and application metadata still exist and group behavior has different trust boundaries. HAI is a personal open-source project, not an independently audited high-risk communications product.
projects.status: Live and actively developed. Core messaging, groups, media, games, Nearby, and PWA installation are available; security-sensitive use should account for the project status and documented boundaries.

projects.summary: A local, memory-aware assistant built with Python and Ollama for personal conversation, decision support, and continuity across sessions.
projects.why: A personal assistant feels generic when every session starts from zero. This project experiments with lightweight local memory so the assistant can recognize a user and recover relevant themes without sending the conversation to a hosted application.
features: Local inference
Run supported Llama models through Ollama on the user’s own machine.
Multiple users
Give each person a unique identity and keep histories separated.
Conversation history
Store prior exchanges so later sessions can build on earlier work.
Keyword summaries
Create monthly summaries that compress recurring subjects and interests.
Relevant recall
Retrieve matching earlier context instead of injecting the full history every time.
Voice roadmap
Text-to-speech and emotion-aware voice behavior are active areas of development.
workflow: Install Python dependencies and a compatible Ollama model.
Start the terminal assistant and select or create a user identity.
Chat locally while the application stores that user’s history.
Monthly keyword summaries condense recurring topics.

projects.architecture: The project is a Python terminal application connected to a locally running Ollama model. Its memory layer stores per-user conversation records and derived summaries, then retrieves relevant context before a response.
projects.trust: Local inference reduces third-party exposure, but privacy still depends on the machine, Ollama configuration, stored history, and any future external integrations. Retrieved memory can be incomplete or misleading and should not replace user judgment.
projects.status: Open-source work in progress with no public hosted deployment. Run it locally from the repository; voice and emotion-aware interaction remain ongoing work.
